title: The Ghost of Vienna
premise: Silas Fairweather, a veteran air-crash investigator, lost her husband and daughter in the unexplained downing of Flight 447 over the Alps—seats in row twelve. Two years later, a routine voiceprint analysis unlocks an encrypted server in Vienna containing proof that the crash was engineered to silence a whistleblower carrying evidence of a transnational inheritance-laundering scheme. Pursued by an assassin working for the dynasty that funded the operation and stonewalled by three governments complicit through silence, Silas must decide whether exposing the truth will honor her family or destroy the last fragile life she has built. In the end she trades her anonymity—and nearly her life—to deliver the evidence at a Vienna tribunal, burying the dynasty's heir and finally sleeping through the night.
about_author: Marguerite Thackeray is the pen name of a former aviation-safety analyst who spent a decade writing incident reports before turning to fiction. She lives quietly between London and the Tyrol, where most of her thrillers are set.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Silas Fairweather, unable to sleep, replays the cockpit voice recorder from Flight 447 for the hundredth time in her Vienna apartment. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief calcified into obsession; she memorizes every second of the recording her family died inside.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Running a forensic comparison of an anonymous caller's voice against archived recordings, Silas accidentally matches it to a dead man—crash co-pilot Tomas Reiner. His voiceprint triggers an authentication handshake with a server pinging from Prague. POV: Silas. Beat: unease curdling into dread as coincidence dies.

chapters.title: What the Server Knew
chapters.summary: Inside the unlocked archive: maintenance logs, bribed inspector signatures, and a memo naming 'the Aldermann trust'—an inheritance vehicle laundering billions through shell airlines. The final file is a passenger manifest with row twelve highlighted. POV: Silas. Beat: cold fury; her family was collateral, not accident.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches Airports
chapters.summary: Introducing Viktor Halm, the assassin, reviewing surveillance stills of Silas at Schwechat Airport. His handler orders 'containment, not noise.' POV: Halm. Beat: chilling professionalism; he studies her routines like a flight plan.

chapters.title: Dead Man Talking
chapters.summary: Silas traces Reiner's last known movements to a Tyrolean safehouse and finds his sister, Greta, who reveals he mailed a physical backup days before the crash. POV: Silas. Beat: fragile alliance; two people bound by one ghost.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Silence
chapters.summary: Silas contacts her old regulator contact in Brussels, who warns her off: Austrian, German, and EU channels all received the same evidence pre-crash and buried it. POV: Silas. Beat: betrayal; the institutions she served are co-conspirators by omission.

chapters.title: Containment
chapters.summary: Halm stages a gas-leak 'accident' at Silas's building; she survives only because she'd already fled to Greta's farm. Her apartment burns with her old life inside. POV: alternating Silas/Halm. Beat: point of no return; invisibility is over.

chapters.title: The Aldermann Heir
chapters.summary: Introducing Konstantin Aldermann, polished philanthropist and beneficiary of the trust, hosting a Vienna gala while ordering his lawyers to 'resolve the Fairweather question.' POV: Konstantin. Beat: elegant menace; villainy in cashmere.

chapters.title: Greta's Ledger
chapters.summary: Reiner's physical backup surfaces: a handwritten ledger mapping the trust's accounts, plus a letter confessing he was ordered to fly the faulty aircraft. POV: Silas. Beat: mourning and resolve; Tomas chose duty over truth once—she won't.

chapters.title: The Interpol Gambit
chapters.summary: Silas attempts a controlled handoff to an honest Interpol officer, Elias Brandt, but the meeting is leaked; Brandt is shot, and Silas escapes with only half the ledger. POV: Silas. Beat: guilt and escalation—the body count now follows her.

chapters.title: Hunted Across the Tyrol
chapters.summary: A cat-and-mouse chase through mountain passes as Halm closes in on the farmhouse. Greta is wounded covering Silas's escape. POV: Silas. Beat: terror and sacrifice; loyalty tested in blood.

chapters.title: The Handler
chapters.summary: Halm discovers his own handler reports to the trust—he was always meant to be deniable. A quiet scene in a Salzburg hotel bar where he begins keeping his own insurance copy. POV: Halm. Beat: the assassin's first crack of doubt.

chapters.title: Berlin Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Silas meets a journalist, Anke Vogt, willing to publish—but Anke insists on verifying everything, costing forty-eight hours they don't have. POV: Silas. Beat: friction between speed and rigor; love of truth vs. survival.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Window
chapters.summary: Silas learns a Vienna restitution tribunal convenes in nine days—the one legal forum where the ledger can enter record before the trust's lawyers seal it forever. POV: Silas. Beat: hope with a countdown clock attached.

chapters.title: Konstantin's Offer
chapters.summary: Aldermann meets Silas personally: full restitution, a memorial foundation in her family's name, if she surrenders the ledger. He shows her photos proving he knows where Greta is recovering. POV: Silas. Beat: temptation weaponized; love against duty inverted.

chapters.title: The Double Cross at the Danube
chapters.summary: Silas fakes the handoff on a river barge while Anke publishes the first tranche online. Halm, sent to kill her, instead kills his own handler when ordered to burn the evidence too. POV: Silas/Halm. Beat: alliances shatter and reform mid-crisis.

chapters.title: Anke Vanishes
chapters.summary: The journalist disappears with the verified master copy; Silas must choose between rescuing her and reaching the tribunal. She realizes the abduction was bait to keep her away. POV: Silas. Beat: despair sharpened into clarity—divide their attention, don't obey it.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes Before Session
chapters.summary: Silas infiltrates the tribunal annex through service tunnels while Halm, now openly rogue, feeds her the guards' rotation. POV: Silas. Beat: breathless ascent; the assassin becomes her unlikely shield.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Climax: Silas reads Reiner's confession aloud as servers worldwide mirror the files. Aldermann's lawyers move to seal the court; Halm holds the doors, taking a bullet meant for her. POV: Silas. Beat: catharsis—truth spoken in the room built to bury it.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Cashmere
chapters.summary: Aldermann arrested at the gala's encore; the trust frozen across four jurisdictions. Anke found alive. Halm, dying, tells Silas he kept his insurance copy 'for someone who'd use it better.' POV: alternating. Beat: justice arrives imperfect and costly.

chapters.title: The Grave in the Tyrol
chapters.summary: Silas buries the original ledger beside Tomas Reiner's restored grave, giving Greta the apology the world never offered him. POV: Silas. Beat: quiet reckoning; truth honored without spectacle.

chapters.title: Sleeping Through the Night
chapters.summary: Months later, Silas testifies at the reopened inquiry—not as a grieving relative but as the investigator she always was. That night, in a small hotel above Vienna, she sleeps until morning. POV: Silas. Beat: resolution; grief integrated, not erased.
